Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

BANGKOK, Thailand (CNN)  -- At least 59 people were killed and more than 200 others injured early Thursday after a fire broke out at an upscale Bangkok nightclub where about 1,000 revelers were ringing in the new year, Thai police said. Rescue officials survey the scene of the nightclub fire in Bangkok, Thailand. Most of the victims died from smoke inhalation or were trampled in a rush to get out of the club. Thirty bodies have been identified: 29 Thai nationals and one Singaporean, according to police. The fire began at the nightclub Santika about 12:35 a.m., police said. Rescue officials said 226 others were injured, including several foreigners. Two Americans were injured in the blaze, a U.S. State Department official said. The official did not release the victims' names or the extent of their injuries but said the department was in contact with them. Steven Hall, a British national who was hurt in the fire, told CNN that flames began to spread along the ceiling above the stage where a band and DJ were performing. But some people appeared to believe that it was part of the performance. "At the same time there were people rushing to get out, there were other people who seemed to be lacking a sense of urgency and didn't seem to realize what was going on," Hall said. The blaze started near a stage where fireworks were being used as part of a performance on the club's closing night, said police Maj. Gen. Chokchai Deeprasertwit.   Watch the fire engulf the building » . "It may have been caused from sparks, but we don't know if it was sparks from guests or from the nightclub's countdown display on the nightclub stage," he said. iReport.com: Eyewitness captures scene of deadly aftermath . Hall said his wife escaped ahead of him, but he got caught in a crowd. "The lights went out, and at that moment, my back started burning, and I was breathing in hot air," he said.  Watch Steven Hall describe his experience » . British citizen Andrew Jones said he was celebrating in the area when he walked up on the fire. He said he saw victims being rushed out on stretchers and spoke to witnesses, including a fellow Briton who saw fireworks being lit onstage. "He immediately ran out of the building, but immediately when he'd done that, the lights went out, and he couldn't see," Jones said. The club is in one of Bangkok's busiest commercial districts. Its Web site features images of bands and DJs performing on both indoor and outdoor stages, and says that it "innovatively blends the comfort of nature with the excitement of the Bangkok nightlife." The site advertises the club's New Year's party, which was named "Goodbye Santika." CNN's Kocha Olarn contributed to this report.

**BANGKOK, Thailand (CNN) —** A fire at an exclusive Bangkok nightclub shortly after midnight Thursday left at least 59 people dead and more than 200 injured, according to Thai police. Roughly 1,000 partygoers had gathered at the venue to celebrate the arrival of the new year.

Rescue workers inspected the scene following the blaze. Most fatalities resulted from smoke inhalation or from people being crushed as the crowd rushed to escape. Police said 30 of the victims had been identified—29 Thai citizens and one Singaporean.

Authorities said the fire erupted at the Santika nightclub at approximately 12:35 a.m. Rescue officials reported 226 injuries, including those of several foreign nationals. A U.S. State Department official confirmed that two Americans were hurt. The official declined to provide their names or details about their conditions but said the department was communicating with them.

British national Steven Hall, who was injured, told CNN that fire began moving across the ceiling above the stage, where a band and a DJ were performing. Some patrons apparently thought the flames were part of the show.

“While some people were trying desperately to leave, others did not appear alarmed and seemed unaware of what was happening,” Hall said.

Police Maj. Gen. Chokchai Deeprasertwit said the blaze originated near the stage, where fireworks were being set off during a performance marking the nightclub’s final night. Video footage showed flames consuming the building.

Chokchai said sparks may have triggered the fire, although investigators did not know whether they came from guests or from the club’s onstage New Year’s countdown display. An eyewitness also submitted images of the deadly aftermath to iReport.com.

Hall said his wife managed to get out before he did, while he became trapped in the crowd.

“When the lights went off, I felt my back begin to burn and started inhaling extremely hot air,” he said in a video account of his experience.

Andrew Jones, another British citizen, said he had been celebrating nearby when he encountered the fire. He saw victims being carried away on stretchers and spoke with witnesses, including a British man who had watched fireworks being ignited on the stage.

Jones said the man immediately fled the building, but the lights went out just as he did so, leaving him unable to see.

Santika was located in one of Bangkok’s most active commercial areas. Its website displayed photographs of bands and DJs appearing on indoor and outdoor stages. The site described the venue as a place that “innovatively blends the comfort of nature with the excitement of the Bangkok nightlife.”

The nightclub’s advertised New Year’s Eve event was titled **“Goodbye Santika.”**

CNN’s Kocha Olarn contributed to the report.

counterfactuals.output:
# Dozens killed in Bangkok nightclub fire during New Year celebration

**BANGKOK, Thailand — Jan. 1, 2009** — A fast-moving fire swept through a crowded Bangkok nightclub shortly after midnight Thursday, killing dozens of New Year’s revelers and injuring more than 200 others as smoke, flames and a rush toward limited exits turned the celebration into a disaster.

Thai authorities said at least 59 people were confirmed dead in the first hours after the blaze at the **Santika nightclub** in Bangkok’s Ekkamai entertainment district. The toll later rose to more than 60 as critically injured victims died in hospitals. Officials warned that the figures could change as emergency crews and hospitals reconciled their records.

The club was packed for a New Year’s Eve event advertised as a farewell party for the venue. Witnesses said the fire appeared to break out near the stage around 12:30 a.m., shortly after the countdown to the new year, while a band was performing and pyrotechnic effects were reportedly being used.

Police said investigators were examining whether indoor fireworks or sparklers ignited combustible material in or near the ceiling. An electrical fault was also being considered, and officials cautioned that no final cause had been established.

Senior Bangkok police officials said many victims died from smoke inhalation, burns or injuries sustained as the crowd surged toward the exits. Bodies were found near doorways and in other parts of the building where people apparently became trapped.

Rescue workers described chaotic scenes outside the club. Survivors—some with severe burns and others bleeding from shattered glass—stumbled into the street or were carried out by friends and emergency personnel. Ambulances transported victims to hospitals across Bangkok, quickly overwhelming emergency departments.

Rescue officials said the nightclub’s dark interior, thick black smoke and intense heat hampered efforts to reach people still inside. Firefighters brought the flames under control within several hours but continued searching the damaged building after daybreak.

Foreigners were among both the dead and injured, although authorities said identification was difficult because some victims had suffered extensive burns and many had been separated from their documents.

Foreign witnesses told reporters that the fire spread with extraordinary speed. Several said they initially mistook sparks and smoke near the stage for part of the show. Within moments, however, burning material was falling from above and people were pushing toward the doors.

One foreign survivor said the smoke became so dense that patrons could not see where they were going. Another described escaping only after being pulled through the crowd, while friends remained missing. Witnesses also reported that people smashed windows and tried to force their way through secondary openings when the main route became jammed.

Outside hospitals, relatives searched casualty lists and showed photographs of missing family members to police and medical staff. Embassies began contacting Thai authorities to determine whether their citizens were among the victims.

Questions immediately arose about the club’s fire precautions, occupancy level and exits. Police said they would examine the venue’s permits, emergency systems and compliance with safety regulations. Investigators were also expected to question the club’s owners, employees, performers and organizers of the New Year event.

The Santika disaster was one of Thailand’s deadliest entertainment-venue fires. It drew comparisons with other nightclub catastrophes in which indoor pyrotechnics ignited flammable soundproofing or decorative materials, producing toxic smoke and leaving patrons only minutes—or seconds—to escape.

Thai officials ordered a full investigation as rescue teams completed their search and hospitals treated scores of burn and trauma patients. Authorities said the priority was identifying the dead, notifying families and determining how a New Year celebration in one of Bangkok’s busiest nightlife districts became a mass-casualty event.
